# Verification Methods

Choose a method that can produce objective evidence before baselining a requirement.

| Method | Use when | Evidence examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inspection | Conformance is visible in a document, configuration, inventory, or record. | Approved configuration, policy record, architecture review. |
| Analysis | A calculation, model, log review, or other analysis demonstrates conformance. | Capacity analysis, cost report, audit-log analysis. |
| Demonstration | A representative user or operator workflow proves expected behavior. | Recorded walkthrough, observed service request. |
| Test | Repeatable inputs and expected outputs or thresholds can be evaluated. | Automated test result, recovery exercise, performance test. |
| Operational evidence | Sustained operation or a controlled exercise proves an operational outcome. | Incident record, backup restoration, access review, monitoring report. |

For each requirement, record the responsible party, verification environment, data constraints, method, objective pass/fail criterion, evidence location, and acceptance authority. A method is inadequate when its evidence cannot distinguish success from failure.
